subject: Re: Urgent: High p99 + timeouts on long-context (32k) for Starlace
body:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@starlace.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Daniel Park <dpark@starlace.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High p99 + errors for long-context 32k requests

Hi Sean,

We're seeing a sharp rise in p99 latency and a handful of timeouts for our long-context (32k) inference calls to the hosted API starting yesterday evening. Request IDs attached in the logs. Impact: our summarization pipeline for clinician transcripts is timing out ~1.8% of the requests and p99 has increased from ~1.1s to ~7.6s.

This is customer-facing — our ops team is getting paged and we've had to stall several production jobs. Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side or if anything changed on our end? We're flexible to take short-term mitigations but need an ETA on a resolution path.

Attachments: request-id-logs-07-29.txt

Thanks,
Olivia
Head of Engineering, Starlace AI

----
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@starlace.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 28 Jul 2029 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 + errors for long-context 32k requests

Olivia — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We’re treating this as an escalation.

Immediate steps: I’ve looped in Karthik (runtime lead) for triage and Marissa for customer comms / credits if needed. Can you confirm the traffic window (UTC) and whether the affected requests were pinned to a specific model or shard? Also any recent changes on your side (batching, retries)?

We’ll do an initial triage within 2 hours and follow up with an exec-facing summary by tomorrow.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

----
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, Olivia Chen <olivia@starlace.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 28 Jul 2029 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 + errors for long-context 32k requests

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Reproduced elevated p99 on a small replay of Starlace traffic against a canary cluster: long-context 32k windows show heavy KV cache churn and increased memory pressure leading to occasional GC stalls and connection timeouts.
- There are spikes in attention kernel latency for certain prompt shapes (very long prefix + many sparse tokens).
- No config change deployed to runtime in last 72 hours; there was a model variant rollout on our catalog that could increase allocation pressure.

Short term mitigations we can apply immediately (low-risk):
1) Route Starlace long-context traffic to a dedicated burst pool with higher memory headroom (requires approval but quick).
2) Enable automatic fallback to the 8k-optimized variant for requests that exceed 16k tokens (preserves correctness in most pipelines).
3) Apply an aggressive KV prefetch and retention tweak for Starlace tenant to reduce cache churn.

I’m running a controlled replay with telemetry attached and will share p99 numbers. Expect preliminary numbers in 90 minutes.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Lead, Serving Runtime

----
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@starlace.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Daniel Park <dpark@starlace.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jul 2029 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 + errors for long-context 32k requests

Thanks Karthik — we can accept the 8k fallback for now if it reduces timeouts. We will validate quality against our golden prompts. Routing to a dedicated burst pool sounds fine for the short term but need to understand cost and any risk to availability.

Please send an exec-friendly summary and a recommended rollback/validation plan. We have our CPO and procurement watching this closely.

Olivia

- Enable 8k fallback for >16k requests and run parallel validation on a 1% sample.
- Offer a one-time credit equal to 10% of July invoice as a goodwill gesture pending final RCA.

I'll join the technical sync. Laura — can you confirm internal approval path for the credit?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Director, Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@starlace.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2029 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary: Starlace long-context p99 spike (attached)

Team — attached is the exec-safe summary and our preliminary p99 breakdown (p99_report_2029-07-29.pdf). TL;DR: cache churn + memory headroom led to GC stalls under 32k windows; applying burst pool routing + 8k fallback reduced p99 from 7.6s -> 1.2s in replay. Permanent remediation: kernel scheduling improvements and tenant-specific retention tuning; target ETA for full fix: 3 weeks.

Next steps:
- Apply burst pool routing (72h) — in progress.
- Enable 8k fallback (>16k) — will run 1% shadow sample for 24h then expand.
- Draft RCA and implement kernel scheduling change (ETA 3 weeks).

Meeting: 2029-08-01T10:00:00-07:00 (30m) — invite sent.

Attachments: p99_report_2029-07-29.pdf

—Sean
